rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent neighborhood-scale massing: one dominant compact volume with a substantial carved courtyard/void and an upper-level bridge-like interruption. The four views agree on the same spatial rule, so it is not view-dependent or colliding across projections. The parcel is respected by the massing figure rather than merely filling the box, and the visible void gives the building a legible public interior. The road frontage/access edge is answered with an opening/threshold rather than a sealed wall, which aligns with the neighborhood-living brief. The silhouette is stepped only enough to produce a continuous sectional gesture; it does not feel like arbitrary cake-tiering. Programmatically it supports mixed neighborhood living/commercial behavior better than a generic object, because the ground plane and central void imply public threshold, circulation, and occupancy hierarchy. It is not the strongest possible section yet, but it is plausible and materially recoverable as an early massing.
